context: Parallel coordinates chart (150 cities, 6 axes, 6 color-coded regions) linked to a sparkline summary table showing per-metric histograms with min/median/max stats; brushing any axis filters both views live.
first_impression: Busy but navigable — the dimming strategy and restrained 6-color palette prevent the 150-line parallel coords from collapsing into noise.
what_works: Alpha-based foreground/background separation on brush selection is well-executed, making the active subset immediately legible against the ghosted remainder; the 6-region categorical palette stays within perceptual limits and colors are sufficiently distinct. The linked sparkline table offloads distributional reading from the tangled lines, reducing the cognitive burden on the parallel coords itself.
what_doesnt: 150 overlapping polylines still produce significant overplotting at rest — individual city traces are untraceable without brushing, so the unfiltered state communicates only coarse regional bands rather than city-level patterns. The legend is pinned to the very bottom edge of the SVG and appears clipped in the screenshot, making region-to-color lookup harder than it should be at first glance.
